content: Hello! how can I help today?
If I receive property from a trust, what’s my cost basis?

It depends. If the property comes from a **grantor trust**, your basis is the grantor’s basis. If from a **non-grantor trust**, and it’s a **distribution of corpus**, your basis typically **carries over**—unless a taxable event occurs.
What if it’s real estate? Can I sell it right away?
Yes, but you’ll need to calculate gain using the carryover basis. There’s no step-up in basis unless the property was included in the decedent’s estate for tax purposes.
Will I get a tax form with the basis info?
Usually not. Trusts aren’t required to issue basis reports. Ask the trustee for acquisition documents, depreciation schedules (if applicable), or original purchase records to determine your basis.
Can the trust deduct the distribution?
Only if the distribution includes **distributable net income (DNI)**. Capital gains are usually retained by the trust unless distributed and reported on the beneficiary’s Schedule K-1 from Form 1041.
